name: Nullthar
description: Nullthar is a selective nociceptor blockade agent that binds to pain receptor pathways in the spinal cord and peripheral nervous system without significantly impairing motor function or tactile feedback needed for fine manipulation. Originally developed for battlefield trauma management, Novafold commercialized a modified version for licensed military contractors. It allows users to continue fighting through injuries — broken bones, deep lacerations, partial organ damage — that would otherwise cause shock or incapacitation.
effects: Maintained motor control and fine manipulation
Continued functional capacity through moderate trauma
side_effects: Injury accumulation without awareness — users fight past lethal damage
Post-dose pain flood when drug clears
Respiratory depression risk if stacked with other compounds
cultural_context: Nullthar has a grim reputation even among runners who use it regularly — the Shelf saying is 'Nullthar tells you you're fine while you bleed out.' Stories circulate of fighters who walked out of a firefight on Nullthar only to collapse two blocks later, having fought through a ruptured spleen. It's considered the drug of desperate people and serious professionals, with very little overlap between those groups. Novafold maintains it's a pain management tool and points to the dosing instructions.
story_hooks: A runner on Nullthar wins a fight against impossible odds and walks away — and dies in an alley three minutes later from injuries they never felt; someone needs to recover the data they were carrying
A Novafold whistleblower claims the restricted formula was deliberately made more dependency-forming than the original military spec, and the evidence is in a distribution manifest
A fixer offers a crew premium pay for a job requiring Nullthar use — the job is harder than described, and one member is already dependent on it
